title: Dresden and Bastei Bridge Day Trip from Prague
short_description: The Bastei rocks of Saxon Switzerland and the baroque old town of Dresden in one day, with your own Mercedes and chauffeur. Door to door from your Prague address, one price for the whole car.
description:
This day joins two very different sides of Saxony. In the morning you stand on the Bastei, a ridge of sandstone towers high above the Elbe in Saxon Switzerland National Park. In the afternoon you walk through the baroque old town of Dresden. Doing both by train and bus takes careful planning; by car it is one easy loop.

Your chauffeur collects you at your address in Prague at the time you choose and drives you north, over the border into Saxony. The car stops at the Bastei car park. From there a short, mostly level path leads through the woods to the viewpoints and to the Bastei Bridge, a stone bridge built in 1851 across a gorge between the rocks. The view reaches down to the river bend and the village of Rathen far below.

After the Bastei the chauffeur drives you to Dresden, about forty minutes away. You are dropped at the edge of the old town, where the Frauenkirche, the Zwinger, the Semper Opera and the Brühl Terrace are all a short walk from each other.

The car and the chauffeur wait for you at both places for the time included in your booking, which is shown next to the price. You decide how to divide it. If you want more time, add extra hours when you book.

The price is for the whole car, not per person. It covers all the driving, fuel, motorway tolls and parking. You see the total before you pay, and the same car and chauffeur bring you back to the door where the day began.

Your chauffeur is a professional driver, not a guide. Entrance tickets, guided tours and meals are not included.
highlights: The Bastei Bridge, a stone bridge from 1851 between sandstone towers
Views from the Bastei over the Elbe bend, about 190 metres above the river
The ruins of the Neurathen rock castle, reached by walkways right beside the bridge
The Frauenkirche and the baroque old town of Dresden in the afternoon
The Zwinger palace, the Semper Opera and the Brühl Terrace on foot
Two very different places in one day, with no trains or buses to connect

itinerary.title: Pickup at your Prague address
itinerary.body: Your chauffeur meets you at the door of your hotel or apartment in Prague at the time you chose. If you asked for child seats, they are already fitted.

itinerary.title: Drive north to Saxon Switzerland
itinerary.body: The route runs on the motorway through northern Bohemia and over the border into Saxony, then on country roads up to the Bastei. Both countries are in the Schengen area, so the border is normally just a sign by the road.

itinerary.title: The Bastei and the bridge
itinerary.body: From the car park a path of about ten minutes leads to the viewpoints and the Bastei Bridge. Take your time on the walkways, the rock castle and the terraces above the river.

itinerary.title: On to Dresden
itinerary.body: The chauffeur collects you at the car park and drives about forty minutes along the Elbe to Dresden. You are dropped at the edge of the old town.

itinerary.title: The old town on foot
itinerary.body: Walk to the Frauenkirche, through the Zwinger courtyard, past the Semper Opera and along the Brühl Terrace. Stop for lunch, coffee or one museum. Call or message your chauffeur when you are ready.

itinerary.title: Return to your Prague address
itinerary.body: The same car and chauffeur drive you back over the border to the same address in Prague where the day began. Rest, read or sleep in the back.

includes: A private Mercedes with your own chauffeur, for your party only
Pickup and return at your address in Prague
All the driving: Prague, the Bastei, Dresden and back
Fuel, motorway tolls and parking, including the Bastei car park
Waiting time at both places for the hours included in your booking
Child seats at no charge: tell us the children’s ages when you book
One price for the whole car, shown in full before you pay
excludes: Entrance tickets, for example to the Neurathen rock castle or the Dresden museums
A guide or a guided tour: your chauffeur drives and waits, but is not a guide
Extra hours beyond your booking, unless you add them when you book
pickup_info: Pickup and return are at your address in Prague: a hotel, an apartment or an office. Tell us the exact address when you book. Before the day you receive your chauffeur’s name and phone number, and on the day they wait at the door at the agreed time.
important_info:
Carry a passport or national ID. Both countries are in the Schengen area and there is normally no check at the border, but police may ask for documents, and visitors from outside the EU need a valid passport and, where required, a Schengen visa.

Wear comfortable shoes. The path from the car park to the Bastei Bridge is short and mostly level, but there are steps on the walkways, and in winter they can be icy.

The Bastei is busiest at weekends and in summer. An early start means a quieter viewpoint.

Many Dresden museums are closed on Mondays. Cards are accepted in most places, but carry some euros in cash for small kiosks.

Your chauffeur drives and waits, but is not a guide. Entrance tickets and guided tours are not included.

faq.q: Is the Bastei the same as Bohemian Switzerland?
faq.a: No. The Bastei is in Saxon Switzerland, the German side of the same sandstone region. Bohemian Switzerland, with the Pravčická Gate, is on the Czech side. We offer a separate day trip there.

faq.q: How much walking is there at the Bastei?
faq.a: About ten minutes each way from the car park to the bridge, mostly on a level path, plus steps on the viewing walkways. It is easy for most people; tell us when you book if anyone in your party has limited mobility.

faq.q: How is the price worked out?
faq.a: There is one price for the whole car, set for each car class. It covers all the driving, fuel, motorway tolls, parking and the hours at the Bastei and in Dresden included in your booking. You see the total before you pay.

faq.q: Can we visit Dresden first and the Bastei later?
faq.a: Yes. Tell your chauffeur or add a note when you book. We suggest the Bastei first, while the light is good and the viewpoints are quieter.

faq.q: What if we want to stay longer on the day?
faq.a: Tell your chauffeur. Time beyond your booking is charged only after a person at Prestigo agrees to it, at the same extra-hour price you saw when you booked. Nothing is charged automatically.

faq.q: How many people fit in one car?
faq.a: Up to three passengers in an E-Class or S-Class and up to six in a V-Class. Larger groups travel in two or more cars. Child seats are free in every class.
